source.title: Concept Component Analysis: A Principled Approach for Concept Extraction in LLMs
source.authors: Yu-Hang Liu; Er-Dun Gao; Dong Gong; Anton van den Hengel; J. Shi

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates whether SAE-extracted features from LLMs align with supervised estimates of concepts, providing indirect evidence about dictionary-recoverable features in real models. It does not reproduce the toy-model geometry experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper cites superposition as motivation for sparsity but does not test overlapping directions, feature sparsity or importance, capacity competition, or one-dimensional feature geometry. It reports SAE-versus-ConCA concept-alignment correlations, which bear on V4. The reported reconstruction losses, activation-patching metrics, downstream AUC findings, and counterfactual feature-variation analyses are not recorded as rows because they do not directly measure the claim version being cataloged here.
record.test_reason: This is a methods paper. Superposition only motivates its sparsity prior. Its results compare its own ConCA method with SAE baselines on concept-alignment correlation, which is the T4 pattern (the study's own method compared with others). The SAE MPC values are comparator numbers with no null control, such as random or unsparse features under the same Hungarian matching. So they cannot show whether sparse features are present and recoverable beyond chance. Nothing tests toy geometry, capacity, polysemanticity, SAE canonicality or feature dimensionality.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors argue that, under stated assumptions, LLM representations are approximately linear mixtures of the log-posteriors of individual latent concepts. They propose sparse ConCA to unmix these posteriors. They report that ConCA beats SAE variants on concept-alignment correlation, reconstruction, activation patching, and few-shot and OOD probing. Superposition is cited only as one motivation for the SAE and ConCA sparsity prior.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains and evaluates SAE variants and a new ConCA method using concept-pair correlations; it does not use the toy-network setup or geometric measurements of the original superposition work.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by SAE variant and model. The paper reports performance differences across model scale and architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: Across Pythia-70m/1.4b/2.8b, Gemma-3-1b and Qwen3-1.7B, SAE features correlate with probe-estimated concept logits at MPC 0.57–0.76, below ConCA variants (0.65–0.81). In a synthetic setting, P-anneal SAE reached 0.635 versus ConCA 0.813.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unsupervised sparse dictionary features in LLM last-layer activations align moderately with supervised concept-posterior estimates, and the alignment depends on the dictionary method.

record.problems: The counterfactual benchmark contains 27 concept pairs, which the authors describe as modest in size. Their theoretical result depends on idealized assumptions that may not hold exactly in real-world datasets; they also note exponential-like activation surrogates only approximately implement the posterior sparsity prior and that underdetermined settings may yield noise-like solutions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional SAE–concept-correlation results from Tables 5–6 were left out. Other reported metrics and analyses were excluded because they measure reconstruction, task utility, activation-patching effects, or feature-response variation rather than V4's dictionary recovery of sparse features.

untested.parts: All parts: toy networks, superposed geometry, sparsity transition.
All parts: capacity competition, dedicated dimensions for important features.
No test of distributed neuron coding, and no test of SAE recovery against a null baseline.
Completeness, stability and canonicality of SAE features. The SAE-versus-ConCA gap is a method comparison, not a test of whether features are canonical.
All parts. Concepts are modeled as discrete multi-valued latents, but feature dimensionality is not tested.

missing.what: SAE vs ConCA Pearson correlation on 23 additional semantic concept pairs across Pythia scales. These results are shown in a figure only, without a table.
missing.versions: none (would bear on V4 only if reclassified)

missing.what: Synthetic DAG experiment: SAE (Panneal) correlation 0.635 vs ConCA 0.813 with known latents.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T2/tests classification and both V4 labels are dropped. The rows are SAE baselines in a benchmark of the authors' own method, and they carry no control showing above-chance recovery. The 'supports' label rested only on correlations being positive. The 'limits_scope' label rested on SAEs trailing ConCA, which is a method comparison and not a scope condition on V4.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, more sparse features than dimensions, dropping versus superposing features, near-orthogonal geometry, and a sparsity-dependent transition.
Whether polysemanticity results from capacity competition or important features receiving dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise for other reasons and whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.

The study evaluates SAE feature alignment on its chosen concept-pair benchmark, not whether features are distributed across many neurons or whether SAE recovery is complete across LLM features generally.
Completeness, canonicality, and stability of SAE features as the model's representation units.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional subspaces.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: SAE methods and models reported in Tables 5 and 6
reader_labels.reason: All reported SAE methods show positive alignment correlations with the supervised concept estimates; see r1–r15.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Across SAE methods and tested models
reader_labels.reason: Alignment varies by method and model, and the paper reports that SAE methods generally have lower correlations than ConCA variants; the results establish partial benchmark-specific recovery rather than complete recovery of LLM features. See r1–r15.
